run.userPrompt:
By 2026, an insurer is piloting climate-linked microinsurance for smallholder farmers in East Africa, South Asia, and Central America. Distribution candidates include cooperatives, mobile-network agents, religious community groups, and fintech apps. Trust in formal insurance, expectations of claim speed, and the perceived legitimacy of different intermediaries vary greatly by region, and actuarial data quality is uneven.

Design distribution and business-model options for climate microinsurance across regions with different trust regimes and intermediation norms, addressing acquisition cost, claim credibility, and portfolio risk.
